**Finding: compliant** (Section 4.4 Audit Rights, ¶p0059) — no redline proposed.

The only audit right running against us sits in § 4.4 and it already lands at or above our preferred position on every material term:

| Term | Playbook preferred | Clause 4.4 |
|---|---|---|
| Frequency | ≤ once / 12 months | "no more than once each calendar year" ✓ |
| Timing | business hours | "at reasonable times" ✓ |
| Auditor | independent, confidentiality-bound | independent CPA **reasonably acceptable to Corio** — better than preferred ✓ |
| Cost | Vendor pays unless underpayment > 5% | Commerce One bears all costs; 5% shift threshold ✓ |
| System access | none | records-only inspection of books of account; no systems/premises access ✓ |

Additional customer benefit: the true-up is reciprocal — a discovered **overpayment must be refunded to us**, not just shortfalls paid.

Two minor points noted in the rationale rather than flagged as deviations, per the playbook's classification semantics:
- Notice is "reasonable notice" rather than a fixed 30 days (or 15 days at fallback).
- Auditor confidentiality is covered indirectly via § 10 and the concurrent NDA rather than expressly in the audit clause.

Neither is a material failure of the fallback, so redlining would spend negotiating capital on a clause that is already favorable to us. Worth raising the fixed notice period only if § 4.4 is reopened for another reason.
